newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro must be launched in 1999 - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Euro must be launched in 1999 - Kinkel.

text.p: European monetary union must be launched on schedule on January 1, 1999, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in an article in afternoon daily Le Monde.

He also said that Germany wanted as many countries as possible in monetary union from the start. "No country which meets the stability criteria in a lasting way will be excluded from the euro," he said.
"The main response of Europe to the convergence of the world economy is economic and monetary union," he said.
"That is why the euro must be put in place on January 1, 1999 as decided in Maastricht. If we do not sieze this opportunity now, we may have to wait decades before it arises again," he added.
Kinkel stressed that monetary union must be based on stability.

"Two factors are indispensable to guarantee monetary stability -- an independent central bank and strict respect of the stability criteria fixed in the Maastricht treaty, not just at the time of joining but also in the long term," he said.
This was why Europe needed its budget stability pact, agreed at a European Union summit in Dublin in December.
"It is equally clear that Germany wants membership of economic and monetary union to be as wide as possible, right from the start," he said.
